s: Which son of Shah Jahan was honored with the title 'Shah-i-Iqbal'?
x: Dara Shikoh, the eldest son and heir, was honoured by Shah Jahan with the titles Shah-i-Iqbal and Shah Buland Iqbal.

s: Mughal Prince who took refuge in Srinagar Garhwal –
x: Sulaiman Shikoh, Dara's son, took refuge with Prithvi Shah of Srinagar Garhwal; Medini Shah later handed him over to Aurangzeb.

s: Who among the following was given the title of ‘Shah Buland Iqbal’ by Shah Jahan?
x: Dara Shikoh, the eldest son and heir, bore the title Shah Buland Iqbal.

s: To whom Aurangzeb bestowed upon the title of ‘Sahibat-uz-Zamani’ ?
x: Aurangzeb gave Jahanara the title Sahibat-uz-Zamani; Roshanara was Padshah Begum. Shaista Khan and Amin Khan were nobles.

s: Name the title given by Shah Jahan to Dara Shikoh?
x: Dara Shikoh's title was Shah Buland Iqbal (Shahzada-e-Buland Iqbal); the other options are invented.

s: Taj Mahal was constructed in the memory of
x: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum), who died in 1631. Nur Jahan built Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb.

s: Who among the following was the daughter of Emperor Aurangzeb ?
x: Mehr-un-Nisa (b. 1661) was a daughter of Aurangzeb; Jahan Ara, Roshan Ara and Gauhar Ara were daughters of Shah Jahan.

s: Khusrau was the son of which Mughal emperor ?
x: Khusrau was the eldest son of Jahangir (mother Man Bai) and rebelled in 1606.

s: The actual name of Mumtaz Mahal was
x: Mumtaz Mahal was Arjumand Banu Begum, Asaf Khan's daughter, who married Khurram in 1612. Mehrunnisa is Nur Jahan's name.

s: Who among the following shifted the capital of the Empire from Agra to Delhi ?
x: Shah Jahan shifted the capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad (Delhi), founded in 1638.

s: Who was the ‘Poet-Laureate’ of Shah Jahan’s reign?
x: Abu Talib Kalim (Kaleem) was Shah Jahan's poet laureate (malik-ush-shuara). Qudsi and Munir were other poets of the period.

s: In Indian history, who was Abdul Hamid Lahori?
o: An important military commander during Akbar’s reign
An official historian of the reign of Shah Jahan
An important noble and confidant of Aurangzeb
A chronicler and poet during the reign of Muhammad
x: Abdul Hamid Lahori was the official historian of Shah Jahan and wrote the Padshahnama, not a commander or a noble of Aurangzeb.

s: ……… was imprisoned for lifetime by Aurangzeb.
x: Aurangzeb kept Shah Jahan captive in Agra Fort from 1658 till his death in 1666.

s: Which Mughal Emperor abolished the Persian Court Custom of ‘Sijda’ which was begun by Balban?
x: Shah Jahan abolished the court custom of sijda (prostration) begun by Balban, replacing it with the chahar taslim.

s: Which Mughal Emperor Started Hijri Samvat in India by replacing Illahi samvat?
x: Shah Jahan gave up Akbar's solar Ilahi era and restored the Hijri (lunar) reckoning for regnal years.

s: Who among the following wives of Jahangir committed suicide?
x: Shah Begum (Man Bai), Jahangir's Rajput wife and Khusrau's mother, took an overdose of opium in 1605, distressed by the quarrels between her husband and son. Nur-un-Nissa, Karamsi and Malika-e-Jahan were other wives.

s: Which among the following is not correctly matched? Emperor Amir
x: Sawai Jai Singh of Amber rose under Aurangzeb and the later Mughals (Muhammad Shah), not Jahangir, so that pair is wrong. Tardi Beg served Babur and Humayun, Bairam Khan was Humayun's (and Akbar's) noble, and Jaswant Singh served Aurangzeb.

s: Jahangir took shelter at which of the following fort?
x: Orchha's Bundela chief Bir Singh Deo was Prince Salim's ally (he killed Abul Fazl for him in 1602) and built the Jahangir Mahal for him, which is why the printed key is Orchha. Gwalior was a state prison, and Dhar and Narwar have no such link.

s:
Of the following who had rebelled against the Mughal Emperor Jahangir?

I. Asif Khan

II. Khurram

III. Mahabat Khan

IV. Khusrau
Codes
x: Khusrau (1606), Khurram (1622-26) and Mahabat Khan (1626 coup) all rebelled against Jahangir. Asaf Khan was Nur Jahan's brother and a junta member, not a rebel.

s: In whose reign was the ‘Treaty of Chittor’ signed between Mughal and the Rana of Mewar ?
x: Rana Amar Singh of Mewar submitted to Jahangir in 1615 (Treaty of Chittor); Mewar and Chittor were restored and his son Karan Singh became a mansabdar. Akbar never got Mewar's submission.

s:
Which of the following incidents took place during the reign of Jahangir?
I. The fifth Sikh Guru, Arjan Dev was sentenced to death.
II. Victory over Rajputs of Mewar.
III. Annexation of Kabul and Kandahar.
IV. Arrival of English East India Company to India.
x: Guru Arjan Dev's execution (1606), Mewar's submission (1615) and the English arrival (Hawkins 1608, Roe 1615) all fall in Jahangir's reign. Kandahar was lost by Jahangir in 1622, not annexed, so III is wrong.

s: What was the childhood name of Nur Jahan?
x:
Printed APPSC key: Bahu Begam. Verified: Mehr-un-Nisa (NextGen, PMF, Britannica).
Nur Jahan was born Mehr-un-Nisa (Mehrunnisa; 'Maharul Nisa' here), daughter of Mirza Ghiyas Beg. 'Bahu Begam' in the printed APPSC key is not her name in any standard source, and Mumtaz was Arjumand Banu's title.

s: Who of the following was not a member of Noorjahan’s Junta?
x: The junta was Nur Jahan, her mother Asmat Begum, her father Ghiyas Beg, her brother Asaf Khan and Prince Khurram. Jahangir himself was not a member.

s: Who among the following was not a member of 'Nurjahan's Junta'?
x: Mahabat Khan was not in the junta; he was its rival who seized Jahangir in 1626. Itimad-ud-Daulah (Ghiyas Beg), Asaf Khan and Khurram were members.

s: Mehrunnisa who was known as Nur Jahan was the wife of
x: Mehrunnisa married Jahangir in 1611 and received the title Nur Jahan.

s: Who of the following was not a member of Nur Jahan’s Junta?
x: Jahangir himself was not a member of the junta, which was made up of Nur Jahan, her parents, Asaf Khan and Khurram.

s:
Consider the following statements. In the reign of Jahangir, Kandhar could not be recaptured due to

I. inefficiency of Mughal army.

II. refusal of Khurram to proceed to that place.

III. difficulties in organising an expedition.

IV. severe cold in Afghanistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Kandahar was lost in 1622 while Khurram, ordered to march there, refused and revolted; the expedition could not be organised and winter made it harder. Inefficiency of the Mughal army is not the accepted cause.

s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors wrote his autobiography in Persian ?
x: Jahangir wrote his autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, in Persian; Babur's Tuzuk-i-Baburi was in Turki.

s: The Mughal Emperor who prohibited the use of tobacco was
x: Jahangir banned tobacco smoking (1617), as he records in his memoirs; Akbar, Babur and Aurangzeb did not.

s: Who among the following witnessed the insult and humiliations faced by Dara Shikoh after loosing Battle of succession with Aurangzeb?
x: Francois Bernier, Dara Shikoh's French physician, was in Delhi in 1659 and described Dara's humiliating parade. Hawkins and Terry came under Jahangir, and Manucci was Dara's artilleryman.

s: Dara Shikoh was buried at?
x: Dara Shikoh was executed in 1659 and buried in Humayun's Tomb in Delhi.

s: The battle of Dharmat was fought between
o: Ahmad Shah Durrani and the Marathas
x: The Battle of Dharmat (15 April 1658) was fought near Ujjain between Aurangzeb (with Murad) and Dara Shikoh's forces under Jaswant Singh.

s: The battle of Dharmat was fought between :
o: Ahmad Shah Durrani and the Marathas
x: The Battle of Dharmat (15 April 1658) was fought between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh's forces under Jaswant Singh.

s: Aurangzeb defeated Jaswant Singh, the King of Jodhpur in the Battle of Dharmat in 1658. Dharmat situated in which state?
x: Dharmat lies near Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh.

s:
Assertion(A) : Aurangzeb succeeded Shah Jahan to the Mughal throne.
Reason (R) : The law of primogeniture was followed.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: Aurangzeb did succeed Shah Jahan, but by the sword: the Mughals had no rule of primogeniture, so R is false.

s: Battle of Deorai 2. Defeat of Shuja near Banaras 3. Battle of Samugarh 4. Victory at Dharmat Select the correct answer from the code given below. Code:
x: Order: Shuja beaten near Banaras (Bahadurgarh, Feb 1658), Dharmat (Apr 1658), Samugarh (May 1658), Deorai (Mar 1659), so 2, 4, 3, 1.

s: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
x: Sir Thomas Roe was James I's ambassador to Jahangir (1615-19), not Akbar, so that pair is wrong. Hawkins-Jahangir, Tavernier-Shah Jahan and Manucci-Aurangzeb are correct.

s: Thomas Roe was received in audience by Jahangir at :
x: Jahangir received Roe at Ajmer in January 1616; he stayed till 1619.

s: Sir Thomas Roe came to India as a British Ambassador during the reign of –
x: Sir Thomas Roe came as James I's ambassador to Jahangir's court (1615-19) and obtained trade concessions.

s: Who among the following was appointed as a physician in the Mughal service ?
x: Niccolao Manucci, who came in 1656 as Dara's artilleryman, later practised as a physician in Mughal service. Bernier was physician to Dara Shikoh too, but books key Manucci; Careri and Tavernier were not physicians.

s: Which British ambassador came behind Jahangir from Ajmer to Mandu ?
x: Sir Thomas Roe accompanied Jahangir from Ajmer to Mandu (1616-17). Clive and Clyde belong to later British India.

s: Sir Thomas Roe, an Ambassador of James I of England came to India in year
x: Roe landed at Surat in September 1615 and stayed till 1619, so 1615 is the year of arrival; he was received at Ajmer in January 1616.

s:
Match
List I with
List II and select the correct answer from the codes given below.
List I
List II

A. Firuz Shah Tughlaq
1. Diwan-i-Riyasat

B. Balban
2. Nauroz

C. Alauddin
3. Construction of canals

D. Jahangir
4. Sir Thomas Roe
Codes A B C D
x: Firuz Tughlaq built canals (A-3), Balban introduced the Persian Nauroz (B-2), Alauddin set up the Diwan-i-Riyasat (C-1) and Jahangir received Sir Thomas Roe (D-4), giving 3 2 1 4.

s: The motive behind Shahjahan's Balkh campaign was to:
o: secure a friendly ruler in Balkh and Badakhshan which bordered Kabul
conquer Samarqand and Farghana, the Mughal homelands
fix the Mughal frontier on the 'scientific line', the Amu Daria
expand the Mughal Empire beyond the sub‑continent
x: Shah Jahan's Balkh campaign (1646-47) aimed to set up a friendly ruler in Balkh and Badakhshan, which bordered Kabul; the idea of reconquering Samarqand and Farghana or of a 'scientific line' on the Amu Darya is the tempting but rejected view.

s: During Mughal Empire, which of the provinces was lost in 1622, recovered in 1638?
x: Kandahar was lost to Persia in 1622 under Jahangir and regained in 1638 when Ali Mardan Khan surrendered it to Shah Jahan.

s: The loss of Qandahar was a big blow to the Mughal empire from the view point of
x: Kandahar was the frontier fortress commanding the routes between India, Persia and Central Asia, so its loss was a blow to a strategic stronghold. It was not valued for resources.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): During the reign of Shahjahan, Dara Sikoh was sent on expedition to Balkh, Badakhshan and Qandahar.
2.
Reason (R): The expedition sent by Shahjahan to the Middle East was a marvellous success.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x:
Most keys: A true, R false. Strictly A is also inexact: Dara did not lead the Balkh-Badakhshan campaign (Murad 1646, Aurangzeb 1647).
The expeditions failed, so R is false. The printed key takes A as true, but Dara led only the 1653 Qandahar siege; Balkh and Badakhshan were Murad's and Aurangzeb's.

s: Who among the following was the governor of Deccan for the major part of Shah Jahan’s Reign ?
x: Aurangzeb was viceroy of the Deccan in 1636-44 and again in 1652/53-58, the greater part of Shah Jahan's reign.

s:
Assertion (A) Daulatabad fortress was besieged by the Mughal forces in the year 1631 and it had to be surrendered to them.
Reason (R) Malik Amber betrayed his sultan during the seige of Daulatabad fortress by Mughal forces.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x:
Most keys: A true, R false. Strictly Daulatabad fell in June 1633, not 1631 (Satish Chandra), so A is also inexact.
Daulatabad did fall to the Mughals (Mahabat Khan) in Shah Jahan's early years, so the printed key takes A as true. R is false: Malik Ambar died in 1626; it was his son Fath Khan who surrendered the fort.

s: Which one of the following emperors had the highest number of Hindu Generals in the Mughal army:
x: The Hindu share in the nobility was highest under Aurangzeb (about 31.6%, mostly Marathas from the Deccan wars), against about 22.5% under Akbar.

s: Which Mughal Emperor was known as "Zinda Peer" ?
x: Aurangzeb, simple and orthodox in his personal life, was called 'Zinda Pir' (living saint).

s: Who of the following Mughal Emperor was coronated twice?
x: Aurangzeb was crowned twice - at Delhi on 21 July 1658 and again on 5 June 1659 after Khajwa and Deorai.

s: The Mughal Emperor who appointed the maximum number of Hindu officials was –
x: Aurangzeb had the largest number of Hindu officials (about 31.6% of the nobility), mainly Marathas taken in during the Deccan wars.

s: Who among the following was called as a 'Zindapir'?
x: Aurangzeb was called 'Zinda Pir' (living saint) for his simple, pious life.

s: The meaning of ‘Jihad’ carried on by Aurangzeb is
x:
Printed key: Dar-ul-Islam. Verified meaning: holy war.
Jihad means holy war – the war to turn dar-ul-harb (land of non-believers) into dar-ul-Islam. Dar-ul-Islam, printed in the key, is the aim of jihad, not its meaning; jizya is a tax.

s: Who re-imposed Jizya ?
x: Akbar abolished jizya in 1564; Aurangzeb re-imposed it in 1679.

s: During Aurangzeb’s reign, whose duty was to see that people lived their lives in accordance with the ‘shariat’?
x: The Muhtasib (censor of morals) saw that people lived by the shariat; Aurangzeb appointed them across the empire. Ahadis and Walashahis were troops and mansabdars were ranked officers.

s: Who among the following changed the Rajput policy of the Mughals?
x: Aurangzeb broke with the Rajput policy of his predecessors by taking Marwar under direct control in 1679, which led to the Rajput war. Khurram, Shah Jahan and Dara did not change it.

s: Which son of Aurangzeb revolted against his father, weakening the latter’ position against the Rajputs?
x: Prince Akbar (called 'Akbar II' in the options) revolted in 1681 and joined the Rajputs, weakening Aurangzeb against them. Azam, Muazzam and Kam Bakhsh did not.

s: The Jat State of Bharatpur was established by?
x: Churaman built the Jat power after 1700 and Badan Singh formally founded the state of Bharatpur (1722); Suraj Mal later expanded it.

s: Who was known as the Plato of the Jat tribe?
x: Maharaja Suraj Mal of Bharatpur (r. 1755-63) was called 'the Plato of the Jat tribe' by a contemporary historian for his political wisdom.

s: The root of which among the following revolt lies in the problem faced by the farmers?
x: The Jat revolt (Gokula, 1669) was a peasant revolt against heavy revenue, and the Satnami revolt (1672) was by peasants and artisans, so both were agrarian. The Rajput, Sikh and Maratha conflicts were political.

s: The leaders of Jat who plundered Akbar’s tomb was
x: Jat leader Rajaram plundered Akbar's tomb at Sikandra in the 1680s. Gokula led the 1669 revolt and Churaman came later.

s: The Satnami rebellion took place during the reign of Mughal emperor
x: The Satnami revolt broke out at Narnaul in 1672, under Aurangzeb (1658-1707).

s: Who was the ruler of Golconda when Aurangzeb seized the fort of Golkonda in 1687?
x: Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) was the ruler when Golconda fell in 1687. Sikandar Adil Shah ruled Bijapur, and Shaista Khan was a Mughal noble.

s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors spent a greater part of his reign to overthrow the Deccan Kingdoms?
x: Aurangzeb spent the last 25-27 years of his reign in the Deccan, conquering Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687) and fighting the Marathas.

s: The Mughal Empire extended up to Tamil territory in the South under the reign of
x: Under Aurangzeb the empire reached its greatest extent: after Bijapur and Golconda, Mughal armies pursued the Marathas to Jinji in Tamil country.

s: Which Mughal emperor captured the kingdom of Golconda in 1687?
x: Aurangzeb annexed Golconda in 1687.

s: When did Aurangzeb get the victory over Bijapur ?
x: Bijapur fell to Aurangzeb in September 1686 after a long siege.

s: The given map refers to the kingdom of :
o: Akbar at the time of capture of Khandesh in 1601
Akbar at the time of his death in 1605
Aurangzeb at the time of capture of Hyderabad
Aurangzeb at the time of his death in 1707
x: A map with Bijapur and Golconda inside the empire shows Aurangzeb's empire at his death in 1707; Akbar's empire never held them.

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
s:
Consider the following statements about the Mughal Empire (AD 1526 - AD 1857):

1. The Mughal Empire was established by Babur after his victory at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

2. Akbar introduced the Mansabdari system to organize the administration and the army.

3. Aurangzeb was known for his patronage of arts and architecture, especially building the Taj Mahal.

4. The decline of the Mughal Empire began after the death of Aurangzeb in 1707.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; 3 is wrong because the Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan, not Aurangzeb.

s:
Read the statements
(A) and
(B) below and choose the correct answer from the codes given below: (A) Not all the mansabdars were military officers. (B) Those who held high civil posts under the Mughals were also mansabdars and were graded accordingly.
x: Not all mansabdars were military officers, and holders of high civil posts were also mansabdars graded the same way, so both are true.

s: The Mansabdari System introduced by Akbar was borrowed from the system followed in –
x: Akbar's mansabdari was modelled on the decimal grading of the Mongol army of Genghis Khan (Central Asia), not on Persia, Turkey or Afghanistan.

s: In medieval India, Mansabdari system was introduced mainly for :
x:
Most books and keys: clean administration. Some guides argue for army recruitment, since every mansab carried a sawar obligation.
The printed key is 'effecting clean administration': mansabdari gave one graded service for army and civil posts. Army recruitment is the tempting option.

s: Military system in the reign of Akbar was based on :
x: Akbar's military system rested on the mansabdari: mansabdars maintained the cavalry, checked by dagh and chehra.

s: Who was responsible for the smooth functioning of the Mughal Mansabdari system?
x: The Mir Bakhshi, head of the military department, ran the mansabdari system (recommendations, musters, pay). The Wazir handled finance and the Sadr religion.

s:
Assertion (A) The Mansabdari system was existing during Mughal period.
Reason (R) Mansabdars were selected on the basis of qualification.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Mansabdari existed in the Mughal period and mansabs were given at the emperor's will on ability, so the printed key takes both as true; selection on merit does not explain why the system existed.

s:
With reference to Mansabdari system, which of the statements is/are correct?

I. Mansabdari system was the official nobility of the state, started by Akbar.

II. A Mansabdari was hereditary.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Mansabdari was Akbar's graded official nobility, so I is true. Mansabs were not hereditary: rank and jagir ended with the holder, so II is false.

s: Consider the following statements about Mughal Mansabdari and select the correct answer by using codes below: 1.’Zat’ and ‘Mansab’ designations were granted. 2. Mansabdars were hereditary officials. 3. There were three classes of Mansabdars. 4. Their salary was paid by Diwan Office.
x: Zat (and sawar) ranks were granted and mansabdars fell into three classes, so 1 and 3 hold. Mansabs were not hereditary, so 2 is false; the printed key also treats 4 as false.

s:
Consider the following observations relating to the reign of the Mughal Emperor Akbar

I. Akbar strengthened his control on the nobility and the army by introducing the Mansabdari system.

II. Under the Mansabdari system, every officer was assigned a rank (Mansab).

III. The ranks were divided into Zat, Sawar and Chehra.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
x: Akbar introduced mansabdari to grade nobles and the army, each officer getting a rank, so I and II are right. Ranks were zat and sawar; chehra is the descriptive roll, so III is wrong.

s:
Which of the following statements about ‘Mughal Mansab’ system are correct?

I. ‘Zat’ rank was an indicator of a Mansabdar’s position in the imperial hierarchy and the salary of the Mansabdar.

II. ‘Sawar’ rank indicated the number of horsemen the Mansabdar was required to maintain.

III. In the seventeenth century, Mansabdars holding 1000 or above ‘Sawar’ rank were designated as nobles (Umara).
Codes
x: Zat fixed status and salary and sawar the horsemen to be kept, so I and II are correct. III is wrong: nobles (umara) were mansabdars of 1,000 zat or above, not 1,000 sawar.

s: Which one of the following is not true about the Mughal Mansabdari System ?
o: They got conditional or Mashut rank
Their ‘Sawar’ rank could exceed the ‘Zat’ rank
All civil and military officers were given mansabs
x: The sawar rank could not exceed the zat rank, so statement (c) is not true. The 33 grades in practice, mashrut (conditional) ranks and mansabs for all civil and military officers are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements: Ahadis were those troopers who
I. offered their services singly.
II. did not attach themselves to any chief.
III. had the emperor as their immediate colonel.
IV. attached themselves to Mirzas. Of these statements:
o: I, III and IV are correct
I, II and III are correct
x: Ahadis were troopers who offered their services singly, were attached to no chief and had the emperor as their colonel, so I, II and III are correct. They were not attached to Mirzas.

s: The troops raised by the Emperor but not paid directly by the state and placed under the charge of Mansabadars were known as
x: Dakhili troops were raised and paid by the state but placed under mansabdars. Walashahi (Balashahi) was the emperor's bodyguard.

s: The head of the military department under the recognised central machinery of administration during Akbar’s reign was
x: The Mir Bakhshi headed the military department under Akbar. The Diwan handled revenue and the Mir Saman the household.

s: Which one of the following pairs of term and meaning is not correctly matched?
o: Khalisa – Villages whose income went directly to the state treasury.
Inam – Land allotted to learned and religious man
Jagir – Territorial assignment given to Mansabdars in lieu of salary.
x: Mauza means a village, not rebellious territory (that was mawas), so this pair is wrong. Khalisa (crown land), inam (grant to learned men) and jagir (in lieu of salary) are correct.

s: The term 'Chakla' has been used in Medieval Indian History sources. This was
o: Territorial unit between Subah and Paragnah, but not
x: Chakla was a unit between the subah and the pargana but not identical with the sarkar; it was prominent in Bengal under Murshid Quli Khan.

s: With reference to medieval India, which one of the following is the correct sequence in ascending order in terms of size?
x: Ascending by size: pargana, then sarkar, then suba (province).

s: What was ‘district’ known as during the Mughal administration?
x: Under the Mughals the district was the sarkar; the suba was the province and the pargana the sub-district.

s: The meaning of word Bantai during the Medieval period was?
x: Batai (bantai, ghallabakhshi) was a system of calculating revenue by sharing the actual crop between the state and the peasant, not a religious, wealth or property tax.

s: Which one of the following statements is not true about Ijarah system?
o: It was a system of revenue farming.
It encouraged the role of middlemen
under this system, land revenue was fixed for the peasant.
The ijaradar paid a fixed amount to the state treasury.
x: Under ijarah, revenue was farmed out to an ijaradar who paid a fixed sum to the treasury and squeezed the peasant, so the peasant's revenue was not fixed. Statements (a), (b) and (d) are true.

s: Who amongst the following is a land record officer?
x: The Patwari was the village accountant who kept the land records. Lambardar and Zaildar were village headmen in colonial Punjab, and the zamindar held revenue rights.

s:
With reference to Mughal India, what is / are the difference / differences between Jagirdar and Zamindar?

A. Jagirdars were holders of land assignments in lieu of judicial and police duties, whereas Zamindars were holders of revenue rights without obligation to perform any duty other than revenue collection.

B. Land assignments to Jagirdars were hereditary and revenue rights of Zamindars were not hereditary.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Jagirs were revenue assignments in lieu of salary, not of judicial or police duty, so A is wrong. Jagirs were not hereditary, while zamindari rights were, so B is wrong too.

s: Which European traveller came to India during the reign of Aurangzeb?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Jean de Thevenot); it is added as option 5.
None of the printed travellers came under Aurangzeb: Hawkins and Roe came under Jahangir, Monserrate under Akbar and Peter Mundy under Shah Jahan, so the printed 'Thomas Roe' is wrong. Thevenot reached Surat in 1666, in Aurangzeb's reign.

s: Who was the 17th-century French traveller who visited the mines of Andhra in search of fine gems and diamonds?
x: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, a French gem merchant, visited the Golconda diamond mines (Kollur) in the 17th century. Bernier, Thevenot and Manucci are not linked with the mines.

s: What is the name of the award given to meritorious men in the Mughal Court in the form of a Robe of Honour that was once worn by the Emperor?

s: Mughal adopted ‘Navroj’ festival from

s:
Emperor Akbar is credited with many initiatives to bring about social justice in the society. Which of the following can be considered as his initiatives towards social justice ?

A. Abolition of Jizya.

B. Allowing entry to public offices of the state to all on merit.

C. Discouraging child marriage and encouraging widow remarriage among the Hindus.

D. Restricting the practices of converting prisoners of war to Islam.
x: All four: Akbar abolished the jizya (1564), opened high office to all on merit (Rajputs and Hindus as mansabdars), discouraged child marriage and allowed widow remarriage, and in 1562 stopped enslaving and forcibly converting prisoners of war.
